sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: Surface display of the membrane-anchored construct confirmed by HiBiT luminescence; CTLA4 ligand-binding function with this specific HiBiT tag NOT MEASURED explicitly in the cited clip.
sites.rationale: The ledger clip explicitly states the HiBiT tag was inserted 'between the signal peptide and extracellular domain of CTLA4', which maps unambiguously to the junction after residue 35 (the last residue of the signal peptide, C) and before residue 36 (K, the mature N-terminus). Python verification confirms residue 35 = C and residue 36 = K. This is a terminal_n site sitting 130 residues from the TM boundary (TM starts at 166), well within the extracellular span. The construct is full-length and membrane-anchored, satisfying the ledger qualification criteria. Full-length human CTLA-4 construct (pcDNA3 HiBiT-CTLA4-FRB*-HA) generated by site-directed mutagenesis to insert the HiBiT tag explicitly 'between the signal peptide and extracellular domain of CTLA4'; the protein is membrane-anchored and surface-displayed as confirmed by HiBiT luminescence detection.

sources.claim: CTLA4-FRB*-HA (CTLA-FH) was generated by overlap PCR of human CTLA4-HA using pEF5/FRT/CTLA4-HA ( 18 ) and FRB-T2098L (referred to as FRB*, encoding amino acids 2,021–2,113 of the FKBP12-rapamycin binding domain of mTOR) from pEGFP-FRB (gift from Klaus Hahn, [plasmid # 25919; Addgene] ( 49 )), cloned into pcDNA3.1 (Thermo Fisher Scientific) and sequence-verified. pcDNA3 HiBiT-CTLA4-FRB*-HA was generated with the Q5 Site-Directed Mutagenesis Kit (NEB) using non-overlapping primers to insert the HiBiT tag between the signal peptide and extracellular domain of CTLA4 into pcDNA3 CTLA4-FRB-HA

literature_notes: Only one ledger line (L1) was provided. L1 also mentions an HA tag on the CTLA4-FRB*-HA construct, but the clip does not state where the HA tag is inserted (the parent CTLA4-HA construct, reference 18, is not in the ledger). Because the HA tag position cannot be pinned from the ledger clip alone, no second site is proposed for it. The HiBiT site at the signal-peptide/ectodomain junction (after residue 35) is the sole ledger-supported site.
